keyQuestions.text: RQ-6.1: What exactly does the freshness signature in runtime/lib/freshness.ts hash, and does a router move out of SKILL.md leave a stale checkout looking fresh?
RQ-6.2: How does runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py discover and parse a skill, and what must change for it to read a sibling ROUTER.md?
RQ-6.3: What does the skill graph compiler in runtime/lib/skill-graph/ index and embed, and does it parse SKILL.md body text, Keywords comments or router markers?
RQ-6.4: What reads the leaf inventory, leaf-manifest.config.json and leaf-scopes, and does the router move change any of them?
RQ-6.5: Does any scorer lane read SKILL.md body text, keywords comments or router markers, and does the router move change scores or accuracy?
RQ-6.6: What do the advisor hooks, the plugin bridges and the routing-accuracy baseline scripts depend on, and what is the fix for each?

carriedForwardOpenQuestions.text: Whether a standalone skill may legally own a root `ROUTER.md` is a policy decision, not a code fact: the contract neither requires nor forbids it, and the replay does not enumerate it. Recorded as a decision for the migration owner.
The accuracy claim is EXPECTED, not measured. Confirming it needs a before/after capture with the recorded corpus and the same empty-database environment.

keyFindings.text: `ROUTER.md` is already a governed root file, but only a hub's copy is validated: the metadata contract lists it in `METADATA_FILES`, requires it for the hub class, and does not forbid it for the standalone class, while the checker runs the root-router contract inside a `CLASS_HUB` guard. system-skill-advisor declares neither `mode-registry.json` nor `hub-router.json`, so it classifies standalone and a relocated `ROUTER.md` there would be neither required, forbidden, nor checked. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:46-55] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:75-108] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:688-694]

Derived extraction does read the whole body, code blocks included, but its writer is off the serving path and the fleet producer preserves curated fields, so the committed `derived` block does not move unless someone re-runs the deprecated extractor. Reading the body feeds headings, body ngrams and code-block ngrams into the buckets, and `SKILL.md` enters `sourceDocs`, `keyFiles` and the provenance dependency set. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/derived/extract.ts:162-174] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/derived/extract.ts:205-217] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/derived/extract.ts:228-238] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/derived/sync.ts:93-99] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/regenerate-skill-derived.cjs:5-19]

Embeddings are description-only, so vectors are unaffected: `skillDescriptionForEmbedding` reads `SKILL.md` frontmatter `description` and nothing else, and that helper feeds the `skill_nodes.embedding` column at both write sites. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:704-711] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:1305] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:1399]

No advisor code parses the MACHINE ROUTER section. A package-wide search for that phrase matches only the section heading and the pointer sentence that announces it, and a search for the `router.md` filename inside the scoring runtime matches only the doc-file demotion rules, never a reader of the section. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:61] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:220]

No live scorer lane reads `SKILL.md` body text, and the five lane weights are stable inputs to any before/after measurement: the explicit lane scores `intentSignals` and `keywords`, the lexical lane scores name, description, domains, `intentSignals` and `keywords`, BM25 weights those same fields, the derived lane scores `derivedTriggers` and `derivedKeywords`, and the semantic-shadow lane scores `description`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lane-registry.ts:9-15] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/lexical.ts:68-75] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:361] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/derived.ts:62] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/semantic-shadow.ts:207] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/bm25.ts:60-77]

Python-side discovery and parsing are router-blind by construction, which is why the move does not break them: `_discover_skill_files` joins `SKILL.md` and requires it to exist, and `parse_frontmatter_fast` reads the frontmatter block, then only the leading HTML comments, merging a `<!-- Keywords: ... -->` comment, and returns at the first content line, so the MACHINE ROUTER body was never in scope. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py:211-228] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py:52-104] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py:84-96]

The corpus driver runs the Python scorer as a subprocess rather than an in-process API, so any change to discovery or frontmatter parsing shows up as a baseline movement, while a pure `ROUTER.md` move does not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/score-routing-corpus.py:27-35]

The daemon watcher never sees a `ROUTER.md` write: `discoverWatchTargets` pushes a `skill-md` target, a `graph-metadata` target, its derived key files, and optional doc-frontmatter targets, but no router target, so even a corrected signature would not be recomputed on the event that changed routing. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/daemon/watcher.ts:263-286]

The doc-frontmatter harvest cannot pick up a root `ROUTER.md` either, because it walks only `references/` and `assets/` and is additionally gated off by default behind an env flag. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:170] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:42-46]

The explicit lane already treats `router.md` as a doc filename in both the doc-file suffix guard and the write-verb doc list, and the Python scorer mirrors it, so the new filename needs no lane change and a prompt like "edit ROUTER.md" is already demoted out of skill mention. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:230] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:314] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:3019-3021]

The freshness signature probes exactly two files per skill, `SKILL.md` and `graph-metadata.json`, and folds both into one hash; a `ROUTER.md` edit alone leaves the signature byte-identical, so `deriveFreshness` returns `live` against a graph that no longer matches the router. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:164] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:168] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:177-178] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:278-287]

The graph compiler reads only `graph-metadata.json`: it discovers `graph-metadata.json` per skill directory and compiles from those, with no `SKILL.md` read anywhere in the file, so the compiled graph shape is unchanged by the move, and only the `derived` payload carried inside each metadata file could change. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_graph_compiler.py:185-240] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_graph_compiler.py:1087-1100]

The hooks carry freshness, never content: the Claude hook and the CLI-fallback helper both read `freshness` out of the advisor envelope and branch on `live`/`stale`/`absent`/`unavailable`, and the Pi extension is a symlink to the hook file inside the skill, so there is one Pi source to change, not two. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:395] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/skill-advisor-cli-fallback.ts:314-368] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/pi/prompt-advisor.ts:315]

The leaf inventory is root-scoped, so a sibling `ROUTER.md` is not a leaf and the two generated artifacts stay byte-stable: `leafRoots` names five subdirectories and a root-level file is outside all of them, and `leaf-scopes.json` repeats the same root-scoped leaf list. The only leaf-side change is prose: the config's `_note` states the router is "the in-SKILL.md INTENT_SIGNALS + RESOURCE_MAP router", which goes stale the moment the router file moves. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-manifest.config.json:4] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-manifest.config.json:7] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-scopes.json:1-13]

The mtime fallback in the same file is only reachable when no stored `sourceSignature` exists, and it compares `maxSourceMtimeMs` against the SQLite artifact; a moved router adds no mtime to that maximum, so the fallback path has the same blind spot as the signature path. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:290-298]

The one real accuracy hazard is an alias, not a file read: `'smart router'` is hard-mapped to `sk-code` at 0.65 in the explicit lane, so a migration-shaped prompt that names the machine router can be captured by the code hub before the advisor's own vocabulary is consulted. This has to be replayed against the corpus rather than reasoned about. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:187]

The OpenCode plugin bridge carries a second, independent implementation of the same signature, hashing `skill:<slug>:SKILL.md` and `graph-metadata.json` plus four `implementation:` paths, so a `ROUTER.md` probe has to be added in both places or the plugin and the daemon will disagree about whether the graph is live. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js:330-344] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js:142-156]

The per-skill fingerprint loop is keyed on `SKILL.md` existing: `if (!skillMd) continue` skips the slug entirely, so a skill whose router moved out is still enumerated, but a skill whose `SKILL.md` were reduced to a stub or removed would vanish from `skillFingerprints` and from `maxSourceMtimeMs`. A fix therefore has to add `ROUTER.md` as a third `addSignaturePart` probe while keeping the `missing` marker, not replace the `SKILL.md` probe. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:162-179] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:131-137]

The Python record cache is invalidated by mtime and size of the discovered `SKILL.md` files only, so it also cannot see a `ROUTER.md` change; this is harmless only because the parser reads no router content, and becomes a defect the moment the parser is widened to read `ROUTER.md`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py:232-241] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py:316-319]

The stage-two replay that already reads a root `ROUTER.md` enumerates hubs only, so a standalone skill's relocated router would be replayed by nothing; whether a standalone skill is allowed a root `ROUTER.md` at all is a policy question the root-router contract's own header reserves for parent hubs. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/leaf-route-replay.cjs:320-330] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/root-router-contract.cjs:7-19]

The three quoted accuracy numbers are a reproducible baseline, not a survey: they are recorded with the exact corpus, holdout and ambiguity sha256 values, the empty-database and filesystem-projection environment, and the capture commit, so the migration can be measured as a delta against the same inputs rather than re-argued. The recorded values are 155/195 at 0.7949, 49/66 at 0.7424, and 19/24 at 0.7917 with tau 0.03. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/scorer-eval-baseline.json:1-46]

ruledOutDirections.text: Adding `ROUTER.md` to the doc-frontmatter harvest. The harvest walks `references/` and `assets/` only and is off by default.
Adding a lane for router markers. No lane has a field for them, and the projection exposes only frontmatter, keywords, metadata signals and the derived block.

Treating the derived lane as a live body consumer. Its writer is marked deprecated and off the serving path, and the fleet producer preserves curated trigger and topic fields while pruning only dead paths.
Treating the graph compiler as a body reader. The file has no `SKILL.md` read; it copies `graph-metadata.json` as authored.
